An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

revisionDesc.change: Transcribed from Liebermann, Gesetze I, by Claude; to be checked against the print.
Liebermann’s Erklärungen (Gesetze III, 1916) added, with his note marks in the text (read from the page images of vols. I and III).
Readings of MS Rs moved from this note to ECf retr 34,2a, the text they are variants of (Gesetze III p. 340).

div.head: ECf 34.2a
div.ab: Post hunc Ædelredus, frater eius, regnum suscepit, regnauitque in multis periculis XXX et VIII annis†.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 662 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann prints “†” after “annis” and gives in the outer margin of the ECf retr column the dates 978–10… (the last figures are cut off in the scan used here).
The note on the London collection’s addition (**) is printed across the whole page; it is given with both columns.
